status: CONFIGURATION EVIDENCE FOR A CHAIN WITH NO DEPLOYMENT OF THIS REPOSITORY. Nothing from this repository exists on chain 5042 and nothing here is authorised to be broadcast. Every address below was read from Arc mainnet rather than copied from documentation, and the reads are cross-checked on two independent endpoints. The chainlinkOracle block is COMPLETE and deployable as written; the smoke block carries launch parameters that have NOT been set for this chain — see smokeOpenNote.
statusNote: This file was created 2026-09-18, after the basket, router, feed, band and heartbeat questions were each answered from chain reads rather than from the survey's first draft. Its predecessor is docs/evidence/arc-mainnet-survey.json, which remains the raw survey and is NOT a config: it records measurements that could not meet the constructor bounds these guards enforce. Where the two disagree, this file is the one that was written against the contracts.

verifiedOnChain.method: Hand-rolled read-only JSON-RPC (eth_call, eth_getCode, eth_getStorageAt, eth_getBlockByNumber) from Node. No key, no broadcast, no forge, no cast. Every age below is measured against the chain's OWN block timestamp, never the reader's wall clock. Each feed fact was read on BOTH endpoints and came back byte-identical, which is the two-provider rule this project applies to chain facts.

observed.usdc: symbol() USDC, decimals() 6, at the 0x3600..0000 predeploy. USDC is also the native gas asset on Arc.
observed.cirBTC: symbol() cirBTC, decimals() 8. Circle FiatToken stack. Resolved by a complete PoolCreated scan of the real v3 factory rather than by symbol search — 26,286 pools across 26,187 tokens, zero window errors.
observed.btcUsdFeed: description() 'BTC / USD', decimals() 8, version() 6, 9,571 bytes of code, answer $81,170.20. Identical on both endpoints.
observed.router: SwapRouter02; factory() resolves to the v3Factory below and both allow-listed selectors are present in the runtime (0x04e45aaf exactInputSingle, 0xb858183f exactInput).
observed.roundCadence: Walked back with getRoundData per feed, 2026-09-18. BTC/USD: 199 gaps over a 449 h span, median 4,352 s, WORST 86,423 s — only three of the 199 exceed 86,400 s, by +7 s, +21 s and +23 s. CBBTC/USD: 199 gaps over 507 h, median 4,531 s, WORST 86,404 s. USDC/USD: 56 gaps over 1,344 h, every one in [86,400, 86,467]. THE WINDOW IS STATED BESIDE EVERY FIGURE ON PURPOSE. Shorter walks of these same feeds returned 16,956 s (11 rounds) and 42,983 s (24 rounds), and each was read as a worst case when it was an artefact of a window SHORTER THAN THE HEARTBEAT, which therefore never contained a quiet stretch. THE 86,423 s FIGURE IS NOT THAT ARTEFACT: once the window exceeded the heartbeat the number stopped moving, and a 169 h walk and a 449 h walk return it identically. The bound is one heartbeat period plus publish jitter, so it is structural rather than a running maximum. See chainlinkOracle.assets[0].heartbeatNote, which must agree with this field to the second.

verifiedOnChain.addressSquattingChecked: THE CANONICAL UNISWAP ADDRESSES ON ARC ARE NOT UNISWAP, verified rather than assumed. 0x1F98431c8aD98523631AE4a59f267346ea31F984 (canonical UniswapV3Factory) and 0x68b3465833fb72A70ecDF485E0e4C7bD8665Fc45 (canonical SwapRouter02) BOTH carry 2,747 bytes of code on 5042 and both fail to self-identify: owner(), feeAmountTickSpacing(), getPool(), factory() and WETH9() each return empty. Neither is an EIP-1967 proxy. Do not populate `router` from a canonical cross-chain address on this chain.

usdcNote: Circle USDC on Arc, 6 decimals, at a predeploy address. On Arc USDC is ALSO the native gas asset, which is the one structural difference from Base worth carrying in your head: a member's gas and a member's principal are denominated in the same token.

chainlinkOracle.status: VERIFIED-ON-CHAIN 2026-09-18 — Arc mainnet (chainId 5042), RPC https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io, cross-checked on https://arc.gateway.tenderly.co.
chainlinkOracle.purpose: The launch oracle: one genuine Chainlink Data Feed per asset, consumed directly. Deploy with DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol, verify with scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs, then set BLESSED_ORACLES to its address for Deploy.s.sol.
chainlinkOracle.sequencerUptimeFeedNote: EMPTY DELIBERATELY, owner decision 2026-09-18, and it is an exemption rather than a dropped field — the distinction is the whole difference, since an empty field with no note beside it is indistinguishable from a config nobody finished. Chainlink publishes no L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed for Arc, and would not: Arc is an L1, not a rollup, so there is no sequencer whose uptime a feed could report. WHAT THE EXEMPTION COSTS, stated rather than implied: ChainlinkOracle._requireSequencerUp returns early on address(0), so an oracle deployed this way serves prices straight through whatever Arc's equivalent of an outage is and NEVER reverts on that account. It fails OPEN. A deployment here therefore runs on two of the three oracle defences — staleness and the sane-price band — not three. That property is pinned by scripts/test/config-doc-truth.test.mjs as a test of the CONTRACT rather than of this file, so it survives this config being edited or deleted.
chainlinkOracle.usdcPinNote: USDC pinned to 1e18 in ChainlinkOracle (the `usdc` above). Do NOT also list USDC in `assets` — the constructor rejects that. A sustained USDC depeg is mispriced by the pin. Note that a USDC/USD feed DOES exist on Arc at 0x84EA90AC252Dc437031461836DB5164219147905; it is deliberately not consumed, and it is worth knowing about for a different reason — see feedFamilyHeartbeatNote.

assets.assetNote: THE ONLY BASKET-ELIGIBLE NON-STABLE ASSET ON ARC. symbol() cirBTC, decimals() 8, Circle FiatToken stack, both re-read on two endpoints. Depth: $7.40M USDC against 73.38 BTC in a single pool, which is $7.40M of the $9.43M total USDC across all 25,101 Arc v3 USDC pools. AMM spot $81,272 against the feed's $81,110 — 0.20% apart, so the feed and the venue agree.
assets.feedDescriptionOnChainNote: The EXACT string the proxy returns from description(). Machine-compared for equality by scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs, and it is doing more work on this chain than on any other. See proofOfReserveTrapNote.
assets.feedChoiceNote: BTC / USD, NOT the CBBTC / USD feed at 0x0baD7926628b6408FeedcABaEc68c1Ea77bd127c that docs/evidence/arc-mainnet-survey.json first recorded. CBBTC/USD prices Coinbase's wrapper; the basket asset is Circle's cirBTC. The two read $81,170.20 and $81,110.58 on the same block — 0.07% apart — and that proximity is NOT evidence they track the same thing. It is evidence that two BTC wrappers happen to be near par today, which is exactly the condition under which a wrong-wrapper feed is invisible.
assets.proofOfReserveTrapNote: A PROOF-OF-RESERVE FEED SITS WHERE THE PRICE FEED SHOULD BE, AND IT SORTS FIRST. Chainlink publishes 'cirBTC Reserves' at 0xEB0884a871ea1f6483B5FC10fd3D7dC5806411fc. Read on chain: 9,571 bytes, decimals() 8, version() 6, a fresh positive answer — the same on every one of those as the real price feeds, and it reports 786.98 (BTC held in reserve) where BTC/USD reports 81,170.20 (dollars). It is the ONLY Arc feed whose description contains the basket asset's ticker, so it ranks FIRST when the feed list is searched for cirBTC. Nothing reachable through the aggregator interface distinguishes it from a price feed except its description. ChainlinkOracle._requireUsdQuote rejects it, and that rejection was mutation-tested eight ways against the real contract including the direction that matters: change ONLY the description to 'cirBTC / USD' and the identical feed is ACCEPTED. So the description check is what saves this, and the sane-price band is not — 786.98 would be far below the band below and would look like a crash rather than a category error.
assets.aggregatorPinNote: THIS PIN IS WEAKER THAN BASE'S AND THE REASON IS A MEASURED PROPERTY OF ARC'S PROXY, not an omission. On Base the pin records the aggregator implementation address, which is how a Chainlink aggregator swap becomes visible — ChainlinkOracle caches `scale` from decimals() ONCE at construction, so a swap that changed decimals would otherwise be silent. On Arc, aggregator() REVERTS on this proxy while phaseId() answers 1, so the implementation address cannot be recorded and swap detection rests on phaseId alone. scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs handles the partial answer and reports a phaseId change as DRIFT rather than as a failure, since a swap is legitimate. The safety verdict stays with the decimals() == 8 check, which is a complete test of the residual AT THE SAMPLING INSTANT. Re-run the verifier on a cadence post-deploy, not only before deploying.
assets.heartbeatNote: 90,000 s (25 h), which is ChainlinkOracle.MAX_HEARTBEAT after that constant was raised from 86,400 s on 2026-09-18. IT IS NOT A CHOICE BETWEEN COMFORTABLE VALUES — 86,400 s was measured to be BELOW this feed's real worst gap, so the previous ceiling false-tripped against a healthy feed, and the contract had to change before any config here could be correct. THE MEASUREMENT, walking getRoundData back on the feeds themselves: BTC/USD 199 gaps over 449 h, worst 86,423 s, of which only three exceed 86,400 s (by +7 s, +21 s and +23 s) and the worst sits 2 s above the runner-up rather than standing off as an outlier. CBBTC/USD 199 gaps over 507 h, worst 86,404 s. The bound is STRUCTURAL: it is one heartbeat period plus publish jitter, and the figure stabilised once the observation window exceeded the heartbeat itself — a 169 h window and a 449 h window both return 86,423 s. Shorter windows returned 4.71 h and 11.94 h only because they were shorter than the heartbeat and never contained a quiet stretch. SIZED AGAINST THE FEED FAMILY'S JITTER TAIL, NOT THIS FEED'S OWN. BTC/USD reached its heartbeat only three times in 449 h, so its +23 s tail is far too sparsely sampled to size against. USDC/USD on the same chain reached it 55 times in 1,344 h — it publishes on nothing but its heartbeat, because a stablecoin resting at 1.0000 never trips a deviation threshold — and its tail reaches +67 s. A feed that rarely goes quiet has not demonstrated smaller jitter, only fewer chances to show it. 90,000 s allows one hour over the 86,400 s heartbeat, roughly 54x the largest jitter seen in 56 days on the best-sampled feed on this chain.
assets.feedCadenceSecondsNote: The feed's own heartbeat, 86,400 s, as distinct from the 90,000 s staleness bound above. Not read by any contract — no oracle exposes its own cadence on-chain. Copy it into the canary's ORACLE_FEED_CADENCE_SECONDS env var to drive the derived pre-trip early warning. UNLIKE THE PREVIOUS DRAFT OF THIS FILE, THAT WARNING NOW HAS SOMEWHERE TO LIVE: cadence 86,400 s against a 90,000 s bound leaves a 3,600 s interval between 'late' and 'stale' for a warning to occupy. At the old 86,400 s bound the two numbers were equal and the warning could not fire before the freeze it was meant to pre-empt.
assets.bandNote: sane-price band $4,000 .. $4,000,000 (WAD), owner decision 2026-09-18. The ratio is EXACTLY 1000x, which is ChainlinkOracle.MAX_BAND_RATIO, so this is the widest band the constructor accepts and one dollar wider on either side is rejected. BTC read $81,170.20 at verification, comfortably inside and roughly 20x off each edge. The band is the depeg/clamp defence, not a tight collar — and on this chain it carries proportionally more weight than on Base, because the sequencer defence is exempted away (see sequencerUptimeFeedNote) and the staleness defence has zero margin (see heartbeatNote). Of the three oracle defences, this is the only one configured with room to spare.
assets.heartbeatMarginNote: WHY AN HOUR AND NOT A MINUTE: the two failure directions are not symmetric. A false trip reverts every NAV-reading path INCLUDING exits, so it locks a member out of their own money while the feed is healthy. Late detection costs a stale price for one extra hour on a feed that only publishes daily anyway — and detection latency is floored by the feed's own cadence no matter what this field says, so the hour buys real safety at a cost close to nil. THE CEILING IS BOUNDED FROM ABOVE AS WELL, at measured-worst-gap plus one heartbeat period, pinned in contracts/test/audit/AuditOracleParamBounds.t.sol. Raising it further needs a new measurement rather than a new opinion, and that assertion is what forces the re-measure.
assets.heartbeatResidualNote: THE RESIDUAL, stated rather than left to be found: this feed's CONFIGURED heartbeat has not been read directly, because no Chainlink feed exposes it on-chain. That it is 86,400 s is inferred from USDC/USD's 56 gaps on the same chain and publisher, all of which fall in [86,400, 86,467]. The inference is strong but it is an inference, and the jitter tail beyond +67 s is unmeasured rather than known to be absent.
assets.heartbeatAtCeilingNote: THIS FIELD SITS AT MAX_HEARTBEAT, WHICH IS STRUCTURALLY WHAT THE OLD CONFIG DID AT 86,400 s — and the resemblance is the thing to not be reassured by. What makes it safe now is NOT that the config equals the ceiling; it is that the ceiling exceeds the measurement. The headroom lives in the ceiling-vs-measurement gap (90,000 against a worst observed 86,423 s = 3,577 s, 4.1%, which also clears USDC/USD's 86,467 s jitter), not in the ceiling-vs-config gap, which is zero here and was zero before. So if MAX_HEARTBEAT is ever raised again, this field does not automatically become safer, and if the measurement rises this field does not automatically become unsafe — check the gap that carries the safety, not the one that looks like margin.

chainlinkOracle.feedFamilyHeartbeatNote: Why USDC/USD is discussed at all in a config that does not consume it: it is the cleanest measurement of the Arc feed family's heartbeat available, precisely BECAUSE it is a stablecoin resting at 1.0000 and never trips a deviation threshold. Its 24 measured gaps therefore contain no deviation-driven publishes at all, and all 24 sit in [86,400, 86,467]. That is what a pure heartbeat looks like, and it is the evidence the BTC feed's own 48-hour sample could not provide.

notListed.ETH: ARC PUBLISHES AN ETH/USD FEED AT 0x50FCDD99D6762D1C170DC6A9111db944AEE6D364 THAT PRICES NO TOKEN ON THIS CHAIN. It is a genuine feed — 8 decimals, version 6, answer $2,606.66 — and there is nothing on Arc for it to price. A complete PoolCreated scan found NO ETH REPRESENTATION WITH ANY DEPTH — and the scoped wording is deliberate, because the blanket form is false: ETH-named tokens DO exist on Arc, they are merely worthless, so one $452 squatter refutes "no ETH representation in any form". Every ETH-named token with a Uniswap v3 pool on Arc holds under $452 of depth: all 52 ETH-or-BTC-family symbols were read and 51 are 18-decimal squatters under that figure, the one exception being cirBTC itself. And Circle's entire Arc token set, enumerated from MinterConfigured and MasterMinterChanged across all history, is USDC, EURC, cirBTC, USYC, MXNB, TRYB and three unnamed contracts. There is no cirETH. A PUBLISHED FEED IS EVIDENCE ABOUT CHAINLINK'S COVERAGE, NOT EVIDENCE THAT AN ASSET TRADES HERE — do not infer a basket from a feed list. The Robinhood Chain 4663 WETH+cbBTC basket does not port, which is why this config lists one asset.
notListed.XAUM: Its feed reports 18 decimals, so ChainlinkOracle's require(decimals == 8) rejects it independently of anything else. XAUM is not configurable without a contract change.

verification: For each asset feed: code.length > 0; decimals() == 8; latestRoundData() answer > 0 and updatedAt fresh within heartbeatSeconds.

DENOMINATION, and on this chain it is the load-bearing check: description() must be USD-quoted AND equal feedDescriptionOnChain exactly. Arc ships a 'cirBTC Reserves' proof-of-reserve feed that is identical to a price feed on every other observable and sorts first on a ticker search — see proofOfReserveTrapNote.
For each asset: minPriceWad > 0 and maxPriceWad > minPriceWad, with maxPriceWad <= 1000 * minPriceWad, and the band must contain the feed's current answer.

sequencerUptimeFeed is DELIBERATELY EMPTY on this chain and the deploy script's exempt allowlist must carry chain 5042 before a deploy is attempted; if it does not, DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol refuses, which is the correct failure.
USDC not also present in assets[].

Heartbeat and band are BOUNDED ON-CHAIN by the ChainlinkOracle constructor: heartbeatSeconds in [MIN_HEARTBEAT, MAX_HEARTBEAT] as ChainlinkOracle declares them (600 s and 90,000 s today; the ceiling was raised from 86,400 s on 2026-09-18 and this note deliberately names the constants rather than restating the numbers, because the previous wording went stale the day the contract changed and scripts/test/verify-chainlink-oracle.test.mjs now pins the verifier mirrors to the source for the same reason); an enabled band needs minPriceWad > 0, maxPriceWad > minPriceWad, maxPriceWad <= 1000 * minPriceWad.
Run: CONFIG=contracts/config/arc-mainnet.json node scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs (exit 0 => may deploy).

smokeOpenNote: THE SMOKE BLOCK BELOW IS A LAUNCH CONFIGURATION IN PROGRESS: PART SET, PART STILL CARRIED. OWNER DECISION 2026-09-19, four values SET and no longer carried: minDepositUsdc 100 USDC, proposalThresholdBps 500, timelockDuration 0, capacityCapUsdc 0 (no cap). See Decisions/Launch parameters set for Arc 2026-09-19. SIX VALUES ARE STILL NOT CHOSEN FOR ARC and this block therefore still cannot be deployed from: commitDuration, revealDuration, executionWindow, quorumBps, concentrationCapBps and proposalCooldown. The owner declined to pick those himself and delegated them to Engineering with roughly a day of runway, because they are a measurement rather than a preference: they were argued for a two-asset basket on a deeper market, and Arc's entire cirBTC pool is $7.40M. Each needs a re-derivation against that depth and the likely membership, with the measurement recorded, before it is written here. Until those six land, treat this block as undeployable for that reason and no longer for the earlier one. WHAT HAS NOT CHANGED IS WHY THE CARRIED VALUES ARE DANGEROUS: they come from base-mainnet.json, and carrying a number across chains is precisely the error this project has already made once - the survey's first draft proposed copying Robinhood Chain's heartbeat on the grounds that it worked there. Every field here is a launch parameter under docs/SWARM.md section 10, so a value is set by an owner decision or by a recorded Engineering derivation he delegated, never by a default that nobody argued.

smoke.minDepositNote: H-8: 100 USDC, CHOSEN FOR ARC by owner decision 2026-09-19 - the same figure base-mainnet.json carries, arrived at deliberately here rather than inherited. See Decisions/Launch parameters set for Arc 2026-09-19. The `<5`-member signer quorum regime weighs stake in BOTH branches since H-8/CM-7 (`headMajorityWithStake` carries a stake-quorum term; `forStakeMajority` is a stake test outright), so dust members cannot pass a proposal on numbers alone. What remains purchasable is the MEMBER COUNT: the regime is selected by head count, so it is only Sybil-resistant when acquiring the ~4 seats needed to flip the regime, or to grief a small vault into ungovernability, costs a materially non-trivial sum. `minDepositUsdc` is the per-seat cost. There is NO safe contract-level floor for this (a fraction-of-stake floor repeats M-6's liveness cliff; an absolute floor equal to the deposit minimum is what an attacker already pays), so it is a documented LISTING constraint: set minDepositUsdc high enough, relative to capacity, that manufacturing dust members is expensive. See AI-AUDIT-REPORT.md H-8 and THREAT-MODEL.md CM-7.
smoke.govDefencesNote: M-6: these three were 0 / 10000 / 0 — i.e. the reference configuration shipped with every named CM-6/VO-5 defence DISABLED. proposalThresholdBps 0 let anyone holding one unit open proposals (the precondition M-7 and C-1 both rely on); concentrationCapBps 10000 let a single delegate carry 100% of snapshot stake and swing the whole tally. Lowering it to 4000 was ALSO credited here with stopping a single live participant plus a permissionless cranker from manufacturing quorum from offline delegators, and that was wrong: the cap binds RECEIVED weight while a delegate's own weight is uncapped (F1), so the binding quantity was ownStakeBps + concentrationCapBps < quorumBps, and ownStakeBps is live distribution no constructor can see. At the values in this very file (quorumBps 2500 / concentrationCapBps 4000) one member's reveal plus one cranked delegator reached 2000e18 against a 1250e18 quorum and PASSED AND EXECUTED, in the >=5 regime and, on forStakeMajority, at three members too. The quorum half is now closed in the CONTRACT rather than by any value here: revealDelegated never touches revealedWeight, and both sub-five stake terms subtract delegatedForWeight (VO-2b, contracts/test/audit/AuditDelegatedQuorum.t.sol). That is deliberately not a config value, because a RuleChange repeals config values and one live voter was demonstrated doing exactly that. concentrationCapBps remains a real bound on TALLY concentration, which is what it is for; proposalCooldown was not validated by the contract AT ALL. Governance._validateConfig now enforces a nonzero concentrationCapBps under a 5000 bps concentration ceiling and a proposalCooldown in [1 hour, 30 days] — the upper bound because an unvalidated uint32 cooldown is C-2's shape on a field C-2 did not cover. There is deliberately NO contract floor on proposalThresholdBps (the validator only requires <= 10000, so 0 is accepted): a floor was implemented, measured and reverted (test/audit/AuditProposalThresholdFloor.t.sol) because the threshold is a fraction of LIVE stake distribution, which a constructor cannot see — in a flat membership nobody clears it, the RuleChange that would lower it is itself a proposal, and governance self-locks (C-2's shape). The proposalThresholdBps below is therefore a CONFIG choice the contract does not defend; a creator who sets 0 re-opens the M-7/C-1 precondition.
smoke.govChosenValuesNote: MIXED, AND THE SPLIT MATTERS BECAUSE THIS NOTE DISCUSSES BOTH KINDS. proposalThresholdBps 500 and timelockDuration 0 are SET by owner decision 2026-09-19. concentrationCapBps 4000 is NOT, and neither are commitDuration, revealDuration, executionWindow, quorumBps or proposalCooldown - those six are still carried from base-mainnet.json and are Engineering's to re-derive against Arc's depth, per smokeOpenNote. The reasoning below is the reasoning all eight were ORIGINALLY chosen under. For proposalThresholdBps and timelockDuration read it as the argument that SURVIVED and is now settled; for the other six read it as the argument that has to be re-made against Arc's depth and membership. It does NOT all have to be re-argued - saying so blanket-asserted re-argument for the two the owner has already decided, which is the contradiction this note carried for three rounds: 500 bps (5%) to propose is a real stake requirement without excluding a genuine minority holder; 4000 bps caps a delegate's RECEIVED (delegated) weight at 40% of the proposal snapshot total (a delegate's own reveal is never capped, F1), bounding how far one delegate can swing the TALLY. It does NOT make quorum depend on more than one participant, which an earlier version of this clause claimed: the cap binds RECEIVED weight while a delegate's own reveal is uncapped, so one member plus a permissionless cranker could reach quorum at these very values. That is a contract-level defect tracked separately from this field, and no value here closes it; 21600 s (6 h) of cooldown is well clear of the 1 h floor and rate-limits the propose-defeat-propose cycle that holds exits in Mode F (M-7). A launch config should not sit on a security floor — the floor is what stops a hostile creator, not what a careful one picks.
smoke.govNote: timelockDuration is 0 here, matching base-mainnet.json and base-sepolia.json — an OWNER DECISION of 2026-09-03 on those chains and RE-DECIDED FOR ARC by the owner on 2026-09-19, so its presence here IS him having said so (Decisions/Launch parameters set for Arc 2026-09-19). A passed proposal is executable immediately, so members have NO post-passage window in which to leave. Do NOT restore a delay here without the owner saying so. (An earlier revision of this note ended by saying the opposite of its own first sentence - that the value's presence here should NOT be read as the owner having decided it. That was true before 2026-09-19 and false after, and it survived two rounds of editing because each round corrected the affirmative sentence and left the negation standing at the end of the field. After changing a note, re-read the WHOLE field and grep it for the negation of what you just asserted.)
smoke.capacityCapUsdcNote: ZERO MEANS UNCAPPED, and that is an owner decision already taken rather than a placeholder. VaultCore.sol:85 encodes it: `uint256 public immutable capacityCapUsdc; // max NAV (USDC units); 0 = uncapped (no limit)`, and :412 restates it at the deposit path. See Decisions/No deposit cap 2026-09-18 — asked twice, the second time with Arc's measured pool depth in front of the owner, and decided as no cap. The depth risk is accepted, not absent. THIS FIELD CARRIED 50000000000 UNTIL IT WAS CAUGHT ON PR 307 — $50,000, carried across from base-mainnet.json, stating a cap where the decision says none. The note below was written to prevent exactly that and did not, for a reason worth keeping: smokeOpenNote USED TO SAY that nothing may be deployed from this block until the owner set it - it no longer does, because he has since set four of the ten values and the note was rewritten on 2026-09-19 to name which - and for this one field the owner HAD set it even then. A reader checks the precondition, finds it satisfied, and takes the file's value — which was the opposite of the decision. The gate disarmed itself at the moment the decision it was waiting for arrived.

x402.note: DECLARED EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN INFERRED, which is the whole reason the guard for this block exists: an absent block already means enabled by default (see packages/chain-config/src/x402.mjs), so a missing declaration and a deliberate 'enabled' are indistinguishable to a reader, and the two must not be. Arc carries the metered read route on the same terms as base-mainnet.json and base-sepolia.json: with this config, apps/api answers every non-free route with 402 and a PAYMENT-REQUIRED challenge until the caller pays through the facilitator, and only the free routes are rate-limited. NO FACILITATOR IS STOOD UP AND apps/api IS NOT DEPLOYED ANYWHERE, so this declares an intended posture rather than describing a live one.
x402.unaffectedNote: This is an API-metering switch and nothing else. It does not touch a contract, a launch parameter, an oracle, the router allow-list or the settlement token: no Solidity in this repository reads it, and Deploy.s.sol and DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol never see it.
